answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on an attestation graph; with honest-rooted starts and capped per-node influence, a sybil set’s chance of receiving trust is limited by how often walks cross its boundary. Its conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S), quantifies that bottleneck, so low conductance constrains aggregate voting weight under these assumptions. Whether labeled zephyr, grove, or ivory, a cluster gains no weight merely by adding internal links.
